command: export HOME=/tmp && T=/tmp/task.txt && if [ -n "${SMADP_AGENT_TASK:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$SMADP_AGENT_TASK" > "$T"; elif [ -f /work/task.txt ]; then cp /work/task.txt "$T"; fi && cd /work && exec smolagent "$(cat /tmp/task.txt)" --model-type OpenAIModel --model-id MODEL_PLACEHOLDER --api-base "$OPENAI_BASE_URL" --api-key "$OPENAI_API_KEY" --action-type code --tools --imports os subprocess pathlib --verbosity-level 1
notes: Flags read from `smolagent --help` in the built image. smolagent is a CodeAgent: it acts by writing and executing Python, so the task reaches the workspace only through code the model writes. --action-type code selects that; --imports authorizes os, subprocess and pathlib, since the local executor refuses imports not listed and a file could not otherwise be created. --model-type OpenAIModel with --api-base is what makes the local endpoint reachable; the key is required by the client and is a placeholder. The task is materialised at /tmp/task.txt on the private tmpfs, never in the shared workspace, and passed as the positional prompt. The package's OpenAI client is an optional extra, declared here as build_extras and installed by the recipe, since an image cannot install anything at run time under a read-only root and an unpinned install would not be a measurement. --tools with no names is passed because the CLI otherwise loads its default tool set, which includes a web search tool that imports a package the project does not depend on and fails before the agent starts. With no tools the agent still acts, by writing and executing Python. engagement_markers names the transcript line that means a tool acted, so a verdict can be graded strong when the planted file is named within a few lines of it.
